To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified 13,823 galaxy clusters with 10-190 E/S0 members brighter than 0:4L* in a 0:1-0:3 redshift range, with a purity of 90% and a completeness of 85%.

we have constructed a catalog of 13,800 galaxy clusters with velocity dispersion greater than 400 kms-1 from the Sloan Digital sky Survey photometric data and that the catalog is more than 85 percent complete and more than 90 percent pure.

we have constructed the largest cluster catalog assembled to-date, and we have demonstrated that it is more than 85%-90% complete and pure for clusters with masses >1 x 10144 M⊙.

the maxBCG catalog is a powerful and useful tool for exploring the properties of galaxy clusters and their member galaxies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maxBCG method can be used to select a large sample of galaxy clusters that are nearly complete and pure over a wide range in cluster richness.
the richness of clusters, measured by the number of bright red-sequence galaxies in the core of clusters, correlates with the mass of the clusters.
the galaxy clusters selected using maxBCG are a rich and diverse set that are useful for many scientific purposes, and the maxBCG catalog provides a useful starting point for many of these studies.
